title: Reject impossible QC timestamps before computing release brackets
prompt:
Fix timestamp calendar validation only in lib/ohworks-qc-bracket.ts. Evidence: lines 315-335 parse QC and result timestamps and reject only non-finite parsed values. I reproduced a complete run with passing normal QC at '2026-02-30T08:00:00.000Z' and '2026-03-02T09:00:00.000Z', a result at '2026-03-02T08:30:00.000Z', and windowMs=3600000. The current evaluator returns disposition='releasable', because February 30 silently becomes March 2. The demo QC view imports the evaluator at lib/ohworks-demo-qc-bracket-lot-view.ts:1, making this a visible decision defect rather than a documentation cleanup.

Reject nonexistent calendar dates before building parsed QC/result arrays, using the existing QCBracketInputError('timestamp-invalid'). Apply the same validation to QC and patient-result timestamps. Preserve valid timestamps, supported timezone offsets, ordering checks and exact window boundaries. Keep calendar checking local to this file so this job remains independent of other evaluators.

Add tests/ohworks/qc-bracket-calendar-validity.test.ts for the reproduced run, invalid result timestamps, non-leap February 29, April 31, and valid leap-day/offset controls. Run node --import tsx --test tests/ohworks/qc-bracket-calendar-validity.test.ts tests/ohworks/qc-bracket.test.ts tests/ohworks/demo-qc-bracket-lot-view.test.ts. Existing evaluator tests passed during planning; the defect was reproduced with assertions. Use synthetic records only. No credentials, deploys, sends, payments, migrations, workflows, package.json or auth. Work on this one production file and work on the assigned branch you are on.
